title: Could Project Kilby Unlock a Data Center Growth Path for TPL? - The Globe and Mail
content: Texas Pacific Land Corporation TPL is using Project Kilby to test whether its land and water assets can support a business line beyond traditional oilfield activity. The project gives TPL a concrete role in a large-scale power development tied to data center infrastructure. TPL shares have fallen 15.1% over the past three months, putting additional focus on whether emerging projects such as Kilby can broaden the growth story. The opportunity could expand TPL’s revenue base, but its financial contribution remains uncertain. Investors therefore have to separate the strategic potential from earnings already being produced by royalties, water services and surface-related activities. TPL entered an agreement to provide land and brackish water resources for Project Kilby in Reeves County, Texas. The company sold land for aggregate consideration of $42.5 million and secured the exclusive right to source aquifer-derived water for the power generation facility and other associated aspects of the project. The structure gives TPL more than one way to monetize the same development. Annual land payments are due through 2046, while the water arrangement could add another revenue stream if the project advances as planned. TPL’s established businesses remain closely connected to oil and gas activity, including royalties, water sales and produced-water royalties. Project Kilby shows how the company can apply its land and water position to power and digital infrastructure instead of relying only on drilling-related demand. The theme is also attracting major public companies. Chevron CorporationCVX is developing Project Kilby, while Microsoft CorporationMSFT has announced a new Pecos, TX, data center campus designed to add about two gigawatts of capacity and support growing artificial intelligence and cloud demand. TPL has expanded its data center strategy beyond Reeves County. During the first half of 2026, it acquired land in Shackelford and Jones counties as part of its data center and power generation initiatives, adding to the company’s efforts outside its legacy Permian footprint. Execution remains the key uncertainty. Management has said these developments require work across multiple counterparties and extensive diligence, and the financial contribution from data centers, power projects and water reuse remains uncertain. Investors should therefore treat the opportunity as an emerging growth path rather than an established earnings engine. TPL ended the second quarter with $248.6 million in cash and cash equivalents, no outstanding debt and an undrawn $500 million revolving credit facility. That balance-sheet position gives the company room to pursue development opportunities while retaining financial flexibility. Cash generation also remains substantial. TPL produced record second-quarter free cash flow of $155.5 million, up about 20% year over year. The company invested $110.2 million in land acquisitions during the first six months of 2026, showing that its core operations can support capital deployment into new areas. Project Kilby strengthens the case that TPL has assets that may be monetized beyond conventional energy development. The upside is meaningful if new data center and power agreements multiply, but investors still lack enough financial evidence to treat that opportunity as fully proven. TPL currently carries a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold). Its Growth Score of B is favorable for investors focused on growth characteristics, while the Value Score of F, Momentum Score of C and VGM Score of D show a less supportive picture across valuation, price momentum and the combined style framework. That mix supports a measured view while Project Kilby and related initiatives move from strategic potential toward clearer financial contribution. Normally, the first thing to note when examining a company's revenue trend is seasonality: some times of the year have stronger buying patterns than others. title: TPL Is Down 15.1% in 3 Months: Is the Sell-Off an Opportunity? - The Globe and Mail
content: Texas Pacific Land Corporation TPL shares have fallen 15.1% over the past three months, even as the company delivered better-than-expected second-quarter results. The decline has eased some valuation pressure, but it has not made the stock inexpensive. The investment case now rests on whether record royalty production and water-related growth can offset commodity exposure, shifting customer activity and a valuation that still stands above historical and industry benchmarks. Second-quarter 2026 earnings were $2.23 per share, beating the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $2.14 by 4.2%. Revenues of $246.1 million also topped the $243 million consensus mark by 1.3%. Oil and gas royalty revenues climbed 53.2% year over year to $145.6 million, supported by higher oil realizations and record royalty production of 39,700 barrels of oil equivalent per day. Produced water royalty revenues rose 20.6% to $37.1 million, while adjusted EBITDA reached a record $215.6 million with an 88% margin. TPL does not operate wells, but its earnings remain sensitive to oil and natural gas prices and to drilling decisions made by third-party operators. Because the company does not hedge its commodity exposure, weaker prices can reduce royalty income and may also curb demand for land and water services. Viper Energy VNOM provides useful industry context. Like TPL, it owns mineral and royalty interests primarily in the Permian Basin and relies on operators to develop acreage without requiring Viper to fund drilling, illustrating both the appeal and the external dependency of the royalty model. Second-quarter water sales volumes averaged 663,000 barrels per day, up 38% year over year but down 19% sequentially. Management linked the sequential decline to weak in-basin natural gas prices that shifted some development away from the Delaware Basin. Produced water royalty volumes moved the other way, reaching a record 4.9 million barrels per day, up about 15% year over year and 6% sequentially. TPL is also supplying land and brackish water resources for Chevron CorporationCVX through Project Kilby, giving its water assets another potential outlet beyond traditional oilfield demand. The sell-off has not erased TPL’s premium. The stock trades at 34.76X forward 12-month earnings, above its five-year median of 29.17X and the Zacks sub-industry multiple of 21.33X. That valuation leaves less room for operating disappointments. Continued production growth, healthy water activity and progress on newer initiatives may support the premium, but commodity weakness or softer third-party development could make the multiple harder to justify. The recent decline has not resolved the valuation question. TPL’s asset-light model, record production and water royalty growth remain positives, while commodity exposure and variable water demand limit visibility. For a group of Chevron's size, the framing of spending plans tends to shape the conversation as much as any single quarter of posted numbers. By setting out a defined range before earnings season deepens, the company offers a reference point that market participants can weigh against its peers. The budget band signals intent across drilling, major projects and lower-carbon lines, and it frames the lens through which the coming quarterly figures will be read and compared with the rest of the sector. A good deal of the attention around the company stems from its continued work absorbing a landmark upstream combination, a deal that reshaped its production base and added a prized position offshore Guyana. The integration has been a defining storyline for the group throughout the year. Layered on top of that is the newly framed capital budget, which signals how management intends to fund drilling, major projects and lower-carbon lines while sustaining a long-running cash distribution program. These threads together keep the name firmly in view as earnings season unfolds. The combination of a reshaped portfolio and a fresh spending framework has given market observers a rich set of threads to track. Each quarterly update now carries added weight, since it offers a window into how smoothly the acquired assets are being folded in and whether the enlarged group can deliver the cost savings and volume gains that underpinned the deal. Chevron ranks among the largest integrated energy companies in the world, with operations spanning exploration, production, refining, marketing and chemicals. The integrated model lets the group capture value across the chain, blending the volatility of crude production with the steadier rhythms of refining and product sales. The company operates across many countries, pairing long-life conventional assets with fast-cycle shale barrels and large offshore developments. This spread of geographies and asset types is a hallmark of how the business is described each time a quarterly update draws near. title: Why Did XOM, COP, CVX Jump To 52-Week Highs Last Week? - Stocktwits
content: Shares of energy companies Exxon Mobil Corp. (XOM), ConocoPhillips (COP) and Chevron Corp. (CVX) surged to annual highs on Friday as oil prices rallied to a six-month high amid growing geopolitical tensions. Brent crude futures maturing in December climbed over $116 per barrel on Friday, while U.S. West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude futures for December rose to $102.40 per barrel. Last week, Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia intensified, stoking fears about energy security and infrastructure and shipments across the Middle East. Saudi Aramco evacuated its Dhahran headquarters after attacks in the country's eastern oil-producing region. While U.S. President Donald Trump said last week that Washington would not be negotiating with Tehran and suggested further developments could follow soon, on Sunday, he ruled out an attack on Iran this week. Meanwhile, though oil shipments through the Strait of Hormuz have recovered toward pre-war levels in recent weeks, with the U.S. Central Command aiding passage through the critical waterways, Citigroup analysts have warned that the recent improvement in shipments may not represent a sustained recovery. UBS analyst Giovanni Staunovo also reportedly told Reuters that any further escalation could trigger renewed supply disruptions. Brett Erickson, Managing Principal at Obsidian Risk Advisors, said in a post on X over the weekend, “Iran is currently launching missiles and drones at vessels attempting to transit the Strait of Hormuz. In a Friday statement, AST’s unit, AST & Science, proposed adding Q/V and E-band service-link capabilities to its 248-satellite network. The request covers selected frequencies between 40 and 51.4 GHz, plus downlinks at 71 GHz -74 GHz and uplinks at 81GHz –84 GHz.  “This supports a deployment model in which the smallest terminal classes can be used by functional mobile user equipment with varying bandwidths, powers, and antenna sizes,” AST said. The proposed services would require compatible terminals alongside AST’s core connectivity offering for standard smartphones. “AST SpaceMobile’s operations are not solely dependent on use of the E-band; AST SpaceMobile will utilize other spectrum, including the Q/V-band and 700/800 MHz bands, for its user terminals in addition to the E-band spectrum,” the filing said. Approval and interference coordination are still necessary, including protections for military users in certain bands. He noted that shares had lost over half their value over six months and recently hit a 52-week low. “Even with that, it’s still priced as if it’s the hottest thing ever, especially when compared with its more established Satcom peers,” he said. Greenberg highlighted an enterprise valuation of 140 times trailing revenue, versus 38 times for Globalstar, 7.5 times for Iridium and three times for Viasat.
